direction-type.words: Preliminary Grade - C major scale - 1 octave
Preliminary Grade - G major scale - 1 octave
Grade 1 - D major scale - 1 octave
Grade 1 - A natural minor scale - 1 octave
Grade 2 - A major scale - 2 octaves (ascending only shown, but all should be played descending as well)
Grade 2 - A Dorian modal scale - 2 octaves
Grade 3 - G major scale - 2 octaves
Grade 3 - A natural minor scale - 2 octaves
Grade 3 - A Mixolydian modal scale - 2 octaves
Grade 4 - E major scale - 2 octaves
Grade 4 - E natural minor scale - 2 octaves
Grade 4 - E blues scale - 2 octaves
Grade 4 - G major scale - 2 octaves
Grade 4 - A major scale - 2 octaves
The same finger pattern used in G and A major scales above,
shown here on the fretboard image, is used for C and D major
scales (2 octaves) by starting on the 8th and 10th frets respectively
Grade 5 - all major scales - 2 octaves (G major shown)
Grade 5 - all natural minor scales - 2 octaves (G nat minor shown)
Grade 5 - all blues scales - 2 octaves (G blues scale shown)
The finger pattern for major scales is shown on the previous page
and needs to be learned for all keys.
The fretboard to the right shows the finger pattern for the natural
minor scales, also to be learned in all keys.
The fretboard to the right shows the finger pattern for the blues
scales, also to be learned in all keys.
